newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close subdued in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close subdued in quiet trading.

text.p: Italian shares closed slightly higher on Tuesday in subdued trading with scattered profit-taking and a lack of fresh ideas taking their toll while a weaker opening on Wall Street also sapped market confidence.
The all-share Mibtel index closed 0.11 percent higher at 12,327 with the Mib30 blue chip index advancing 0.07 percent to 18,404.
A mood of caution gripped most investors ahead of the unveiling of the government's three-year economic strategy, expected later this month.

Generali and Alleanza bounded ahead on the back of strong 1996 results, published on Monday evening. Generali closed 3.02 percent higher at 30,656 lire with Alleanza finishing 3.96 percent at 12,252 lire.

Investors reacted to news that a 20.5 percent stake in cement producer Unicem would be sold by Agnelli family holding company IFIL to Fratelli Buzzi at 18,800 lire a share for 245 billion lire by marking up IFIL shares.
Unicem shares had been suspended before the market opened pending an announcement.
IFIL stock closed 3.15 percent higher at 5,235 lire while shares in IFI, which has a stake in Unicem, closed 1.39 percent up at 20,936 lire.
Eni and Fiat were both hit by profit-taking and closed fractionally lower, Fiat shedding 0.19 percent to end at 5,706 lire and ENI closing 0.09 percent lower at 8,734 lire.
